# University of the Andes (Colombia)
The University of the Andes (Universidad de los Andes) was founded in 1948 in Bogotá by Mario Laserna Pinzón as Colombia's first nonsectarian and non-politically affiliated university, modeled after the American university system. Its mission focuses on fostering pluralism, diversity, and academic excellence while maintaining neutrality amid Colombia's political turbulence. Early on, the university implemented innovative programs such as the "three/two" route allowing students to complete undergraduate studies at Uniandes and partner U.S. institutions, and developed interdisciplinary curricula that enable students to tailor their educational paths.
Today, Uniandes comprises 10 faculties and multiple academic units, supporting a diverse student body and faculty—70% of whom hold PhDs from top universities globally. Located in Bogotá’s historic center, its campus blends restored industrial and religious buildings with modern facilities, offering more than 445,000 books, specialized libraries, and extensive sports amenities. The university is recognized for its rigorous academics, international exchange partnerships with over 119 universities, and highly selective admissions, attracting top-performing students nationwide. Notable alumni include former Colombian presidents, government ministers, artists, scientists, and influential figures across various fields.
